name: Paul Thompson
current_positions: Radio New Zealand (RNZ) 首席执行官兼总编辑

education.notes: Bachelor's degree in History from Massey University

work_experience.title: Chief Executive and Editor-in-Chief
work_experience.organization: 新西蘭國家廣播電台(Radio New Zealand)
work_experience.description: Led RNZ's transformation from a traditional radio broadcaster into a multimedia public media organisation reaching over 80% of the New Zealand public. Under his leadership, RNZ expanded its digital presence, launched content sharing partnerships with multiple media outlets, introduced Chinese and Hindi language news portals, and became New Zealand's most trusted news brand. Oversaw the organisation through funding challenges including consecutive budget cuts in 2025 (NZ$4.6M) and 2026 (NZ$1.4M). Will depart at the end of 2026.

work_experience.title: Group Executive Editor
work_experience.description: Editor-in-Chief of Fairfax Media New Zealand (now Stuff Ltd) with responsibility for all Fairfax journalism across New Zealand. Oversaw the editorial direction of major titles including The Press, The Dominion Post, The Sunday Star-Times, and Stuff.co.nz.

work_experience.title: Editor
work_experience.description: Editor of The Press, Christchurch's major daily newspaper. Notably on September 11, 2001, made the decision to stop the printing presses to add breaking news of the terrorist attacks to the front page, and at 2am decided to publish an afternoon edition dedicated to the event - the first time in the newspaper's history.

work_experience.title: Journalist
work_experience.description: Joined The Press as a journalist in 1995, working as a reporter and sub-editor before advancing to editorial leadership roles

work_experience.notes: Chief Executive and Editor-in-Chief of New Zealand's public service broadcaster since September 2013. Announced in May 2026 that he will leave the organisation at the end of 2026 after 13 years in the role.
Elected President of the Public Media Alliance (formerly Commonwealth Broadcasting Association) in September 2016, the leading international consortium of public service broadcasters

biography_summary: 保罗·汤普森（Paul Thompson）是新西兰资深媒体高管，1966年或1967年出生，自2013年9月起担任新西兰国家广播电台（RNZ）首席执行官兼总编辑超过13年，是新西兰主要媒体公司中任期最长的首席执行官。2026年5月22日宣布将于年底离职。汤普森拥有梅西大学历史学学士学位（1987-1989年）。他的新闻职业生涯始于1995年加入基督城《新闻报》（The Press）担任记者。2001年晋升为《新闻报》总编辑，任期内最具标志性的事件是2001年9月11日恐怖袭击发生时，他果断决定停机重印头版加入突发新闻，并在凌晨2点决定出版午间特刊——这是该报历史上首次发行午间版。2007年11月，汤普森升任费尔法克斯媒体集团（Fairfax Media，现Stuff有限公司）新西兰区执行总编辑，负责集团旗下所有刊物的编辑方向。2013年9月，他从费尔法克斯转任RNZ，被聘用来升级其数字媒体业务。在他的领导下，RNZ从传统广播电台成功转型为多媒体公共广播机构，受众覆盖超过80%的新西兰公众。他推动建立了创新性的内容共享模式，使RNZ内容能够通过多个合作伙伴平台分发，并推出了中文和印度语新闻门户。2016年9月，汤普森当选为国际公共媒体联盟（Public Media Alliance）主席，在全球范围内倡导公共服务媒体的重要性。然而，他的任期也面临重大挑战：2023年RNZ爆发国际新闻编辑不当事件，2025年和2026年连续遭受政府拨款削减，累计削减超过600万纽币。2025年12月，汤普森向董事会表达了离职意向，2026年5月正式公布。董事会主席吉姆·马瑟赞扬他在13年任期内表现出色，带领RNZ完成了向多媒体公共媒体机构的艰难转型，使RNZ的影响力和覆盖面达到历史最高水平。媒体部长保罗·戈德史密斯也对他表示感谢。
